verified_facts.text: Paradero Todos Santos is located between Todos Santos and Pescadero on the Baja California Sur coast of Mexico.
verified_facts.excerpt: Located between Todos Santos and Pescadero, Paradero Todos Santos is conveniently accessible from three nearby airports, each approximately one hour away:

verified_facts.text: Three airports (Los Cabos SJD, La Paz LAP and Cabo San Lucas CSL) are each approximately one hour away.
verified_facts.excerpt: Located between Todos Santos and Pescadero, Paradero Todos Santos is conveniently accessible from three nearby airports, each approximately one hour away:

verified_facts.text: The hotel is defined by the five distinct ecosystems that surround it.
verified_facts.excerpt: defined by the five distinct ecosystems that surround it and the ancient rituals shaped over generations

verified_facts.text: Every suite has a private terrace, an indoor-outdoor rain shower, air conditioning, Wi-Fi, blackout drapes and an in-room safe.
verified_facts.excerpt: Every suite has a private terrace, indoor-outdoor rain shower, A/C, Wi-Fi, blackout drapes, and an in-room safe.

verified_facts.text: The Mountain View Sky Suite faces the Sierra de la Laguna, farmland and the ocean horizon.
verified_facts.excerpt: The Mountain View faces the Sierra de la Laguna, farmland, and the ocean horizon.

verified_facts.text: The Saguaro Suite spans three levels on a corner lot with views of the Sierra de la Laguna mountains, Las Palmas Beach and the La Mesa farming fields.
verified_facts.excerpt: A corner position that produces views unavailable from anywhere else on the property: the Sierra de la Laguna mountains, Las Palmas Beach, and La Mesa farming fields simultaneously.

verified_facts.text: The ground-floor Garden Suite Hammock opens onto a Japanese-inspired desert zen garden with an artisan-made hammock.
verified_facts.excerpt: The Garden Suite Hammock (640 sq ft) is ground-floor, opening onto a Japanese-inspired desert zen garden with an artisan hammock.

verified_facts.text: The Garden Suite design draws from Mexican hacienda heritage and Japanese spatial minimalism.
verified_facts.excerpt: The design draws from both Mexican hacienda heritage and Japanese spatial minimalism.

verified_facts.text: The Ojo de Agua Spa draws on the healing traditions of Mexico and the stillness of the Baja landscape.
verified_facts.excerpt: we invite you to relax at our Ojo de Agua Spa. Where practices and services draw from the healing traditions of Mexico and the stillness of the Baja landscape.

verified_facts.text: A traditional temazcal and sound healing are complimentary for Paradero Unbound guests.
verified_facts.excerpt:
Complimentary experiences for Paradero Unbound guests

Traditional Temazcal

verified_facts.text: The all-inclusive Paradero Unbound rate includes breakfast, lunch and dinner, access to experiences, breathwork, sound healing and horseback riding.
verified_facts.excerpt: Destination-driven dining, immersive experiences, and transportation are thoughtfully included.

verified_facts.text: Dining uses local ingredients sourced from the hotel's living milpa, which helps restore Baja's native ecosystem.
verified_facts.excerpt: With local ingredients sourced from our living milpa that helps restore Baja

verified_facts.text: Experiences are land-led journeys across the five ecosystems that surround Paradero.
verified_facts.excerpt: Land-led journeys across the five ecosystems that surround Paradero, guided by rituals shaped over generations.

verified_facts.text: Architects Ruben Valdez and Yashar Yektajo designed desert-hued, brutalist-inflected structures around a 100,000-square-foot botanical garden of endemic plants.
verified_facts.excerpt: The result is a series of desert-hued, brutalist-inflected structures that surround a 100,000-square-foot botanical garden where endemic plants like red sand verbena, Mojave yucca, and Shaw

verified_facts.text: The hotel is not beachfront; the Pacific is a solid hike or short drive away.
verified_facts.excerpt: The hotel isn’t beachfront, like many in the area are, but rather a solid hike or short drive to the Pacific.

verified_facts.text: The Ojo de Agua spa has hot and cold dipping pools and is shaded by almost 100 palm trees.
verified_facts.excerpt: Shaded by almost 100 palm trees and other endemic plants, the Ojo de Agua (watering hole) spa has hot and cold dipping pools.

verified_facts.text: Rooms have no TVs or phones, and there is no room service.
verified_facts.excerpt: The rooms don’t have TVs, or even phones to call for room service (they don’t offer it).

verified_facts.text: The property has an infinity pool and an open-air common area called the living room, with hammocks and rattan lounge pillows.
verified_facts.excerpt: the spa, infinity pool, and the open-air common area known as the living room (hammocks, rattan lounge pillows)

verified_facts.text: The restaurant is led by chef Eduardo Rios, an alum of Pujol in Mexico City.
verified_facts.excerpt: Led by chef Eduardo Ríos—an alum of Enrique Olvera’s Mexico City restaurant, Pujol—the restaurant turns out classic seafood dishes like chocolata clams and fried soft shell crab tacos.

verified_facts.text: Pets are welcome with prior notice to the reservations team and applicable charges.
verified_facts.excerpt: Pets are welcome with prior notice to the reservations team and applicable charges.

verified_facts.text: The town of Todos Santos is about a 15-minute car ride away.
verified_facts.excerpt: The nearby town of Todos Santos, about a 15-minute car ride away, is small but offers a cultural punch
